properties.title: Failure Detection for Surgical Robot Imitation Policies via Flow-Matching World Modeling

properties.review_access: Full nine-page text and earlier API page-image review notes; this synthesis received no images directly.

properties.design: Offline failure-detector evaluation on recorded policy executions.
properties.membership_assessment: Implemented persistent scene history and learned procedural-world transition satisfy core-method identity. The evaluated application is a supporting monitoring component.
properties.clinical_boundary: Simulation and physical dVRK manipulation, not established human clinical validation.

properties.name: FoMo-FD
properties.identity_boundary: Reported method/configuration across task-specific experiments, not an identified single shared weights artifact. Exact task-specific checkpoint identities are not reported.
properties.encoder: Frozen DINOv2 followed by frozen per-view feature-space beta-VAE posterior means.
properties.transition: Conditional flow-matching endpoint distribution given visual history and intervening commanded actions.
properties.backbone: View-specific spatiotemporal transformer branches; shared action conditioner.
properties.transport_coordinate: Generative transport coordinate tau, distinct from robot or clinical time.
properties.recursive_rollout: The described endpoint operation is explicitly non-autoregressive.

properties.flow: Images → DINOv2 → per-view VAE means → latent history plus commanded-action chunk → inverse transport of observed endpoint → normalized base-space score → per-view conformal threshold → alarm.
properties.views: Independently scored fixed and wrist views; no demonstrated alarm fusion.
properties.host_policy: Separate imitation-trained ACT policy per task.
properties.policy_coupling: FoMo-FD monitors executions; no world-model-based action optimization or host-policy training is reported.
properties.execution: Offline detector evaluation without online intervention.

properties.purpose: Research evaluation of low-level surgical-robot execution inconsistency detection.
properties.population: Recorded task-specific policy executions; not an identified patient cohort.
properties.environment: Isaac Sim and physical dVRK manipulation setups.
properties.decision_point: After observing the endpoint of a visual-action window.
properties.authority: Offline alarm classification; no remedial action execution.

properties.input: Fixed and wrist images resized to 224×224.
Latent history, commanded-action chunk, transport state and transport coordinate.
properties.output: Conditional transport velocity defining an endpoint distribution.
properties.boundary: Direct endpoint prediction, not recursive procedure simulation.

properties.responsibility: Selected M9 scoring, calibration and alarm functions.
properties.score: Squared norm of the inverse-transported endpoint normalized by Gaussian-base scale.
properties.threshold: Per-view conformal order statistic of successful-episode maximum scores.
properties.boundary: Alarm discrimination is evaluated; live protective response is not.

properties.name: Task-specific expert demonstrations and recorded ACT-policy rollouts
properties.version: As described in the pinned preprint; immutable data release not identified.

properties.FDR: Failure detection rate: fraction of failed rollouts with at least one threshold exceedance.
properties.FAR: False alarm rate: fraction of successful rollouts with at least one threshold exceedance.
properties.calibration: N=19 successful rollouts per task; alpha=0.05; episode maxima; independent views.
properties.controls: Same compressed features, calibration protocol and evaluation splits.

properties.endpoint: Offline alarm discrimination, not forecast-state fidelity or intervention utility.
properties.aggregation: Pooled task-specific experiments, reported separately by camera.

properties.endpoint: FDR/FAR, not matched alternative-command successor predictions.
properties.artifact_identity: Separate ablation configurations; exact trained checkpoints not reported.

properties.measurement: Visual encoding plus inverse ODE scoring.

evidence_fragments.content:
Failure Detection for Surgical Robot Imitation Policies via
Flow-Matching World Modeling
Zhefeng Huang 1, Yilin Cai 1, Ankit Patel 2, Mohammad Hajiha 3, Brendan Browne 3, Yue Chen 4
This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication.

Source code, trained models, and processed
datasets will be released upon acceptance.

Rather than recursively predicting
the next frame, FoMo-FD predicts the endpoint latent of
a short observation window conditioned on the preceding
observation history and the intervening robot actions.

The goal is to learn a runtime failure detector that monitors
execution and raises an alarm when behavior deviates from
nominal successful execution.

Following VFMF, we compress the
DINOv2 patch feature with an offline-trained variational
autoencoder (V AE) and train the flow-matching world model
on the resulting compact latent tensor.

After training,
the V AE is frozen, and we use the deterministic posterior
mode

This regularizer discourages information from
concentrating in only a few latent channels.

[paraphrase of Equation (2)] The feature-space VAE objective combines squared reconstruction error against DINOv2 features, beta-weighted Gaussian KL regularization and gamma-weighted channel-utilization regularization.

First, we condition the flow-matching backbone on the
intervening robot actions. Second, instead of autoregressively
predicting future latents, we predict the endpoint latent of a
short execution window. This endpoint formulation captures
visual-action consistency over the window with a single
prediction for each nonconformity score.

[paraphrase of Equations (3)–(5)] Each view's nominal endpoint distribution is conditioned on L observed visual latents and actions from t through t+K−1. A Gaussian base is linearly interpolated to the observed t+K endpoint using transport coordinate tau. Squared vector-field error against endpoint-minus-base velocity trains the conditional flow.

and processes them with a transformer backbone using
temporal attention over the history dimension and spatial
attention over the latent tensor. The visual branches are view-
specific, while the action conditioner is shared across views.

provides action tokens for cross-
attention and a global action embedding for adaptive mod-
ulation.

[paraphrase of Equations (6)–(7) and their adjacent description] The full dynamics objective combines endpoint flow matching and an auxiliary squared-error next-latent prediction loss. The auxiliary head is used only during training, not for test-time nonconformity scoring.

[paraphrase of the contiguous scoring specification, Equations (8)–(9)] The observed endpoint at t is inverse-transported from tau=1 to tau=0 under the context ending at t−K. The score is the squared norm of the recovered base variable after division by sigma. No sampled future prediction is required.

In our
implementation, scores are computed separately for each
view and monitored independently.

[paraphrase of Equation (10) and its adjacent calibration specification] Successful-episode peak scores are sorted separately by view. The threshold uses index ceil((N+1)(1−alpha)); a score strictly greater than the view-specific threshold raises an alarm.

The needle-pickup and ring-over-
post experiments are conducted in NVIDIA Isaac Sim using
anatomically realistic organ scenes adapted from the SuFIA-
BC environment [30]. During demonstration collection, a
physical dVRK master tool manipulator (MTM) is used to
teleoperate the simulated patient-side manipulator (PSM).
The tissue-retraction and shunt-insertion experiments are
conducted on a physical dVRK.

For each task, we train a
separate Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) policy [31]
from teleoperated expert demonstrations.

[paraphrase of the contiguous preprocessing/VAE-training passage] Images are resized to 224×224. View-specific VAEs use DINOv2 features from the expert demonstrations with beta=0.01 and channel-utilization weight gamma=0.5. They are frozen before deterministic posterior-mode encoding.

locator.section_or_table: IV.A continuation; latent-shape equality begins at end of physical page 4

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase of the configuration passage continued from physical page 4] Per-view latent height and width are 16 with 8 channels. Main history length L=4 and endpoint gap K=4 give H=8 monitored steps. Loss weights are lambda_FM=1.0 and lambda_aux=0.5.

After training both the policy
and the world model, we evaluate the detector on policy
rollouts: successful policy rollouts are split into a calibration
set and a held-out set for FAR evaluation, while failed
policy rollouts are reserved for FDR evaluation. Thus, policy
rollouts are used for threshold calibration and evaluation, not
for training the world model.

For each task, we useN= 19successful policy rollouts
for conformal calibration and setα= 0.05for all detector
configurations. The calibration rollouts are disjoint from
the evaluation rollouts.

For rollout-level evaluation, each
simulated task includes 20 failed policy rollouts per failure
mode and 20 held-out successful policy rollouts. Each real-
world task includes 10 failed policy rollouts per failure
mode and 20 held-out successful policy rollouts. In total, the
evaluation set contains 320 failed rollouts and 80 successful
rollouts. A failed rollout is counted as detected if the score
for the evaluated view exceeds its calibrated threshold at least
once during the rollout; a successful rollout is counted as a
false alarm under the same criterion.

However, the results reported here are computed
offline and do not involve online intervention.

On a desktop workstation with an Intel
Core Ultra 9 285K CPU, an NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU, and
64 GB RAM, the detector processes scoring windows at
13.98 Hz. This exceeds the 10 Hz policy and observation
loop used in the real-world experiments, suggesting that
the scoring pipeline is computationally feasible for online
monitoring.

[paraphrase of the Baselines paragraph] WM-NC uses inverse-base-space distance; WM-PE uses the same world model with deterministic endpoint prediction error. Adapted logpZO and RND use the same VAE-compressed visual features. Detector configurations share conformal calibration and evaluation rollout splits.

[paraphrase of Table I aggregate rows] Column order is WM-NC fixed/wrist, logpZO fixed/wrist, RND fixed/wrist, WM-PE fixed/wrist. Overall FAR percentages: 10.0, 1.3, 0.0, 3.8, 0.0, 1.3, 3.8, 7.5. Overall FDR percentages: 45.9, 96.6, 34.4, 45.3, 37.8, 42.8, 16.9, 52.2.

locator.section_or_table: Table I, task labels and selected rows

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase of Table I] Needle Pickup and Ring Over Post are simulated; Tissue Retraction and Shunt Insertion are physical experiments. WM-NC fixed/wrist detections are 1/20 and 20/20 for Needle Pickup OOD Initial Condition, 1/20 and 20/20 for Execution Mismatch, 1/20 and 16/20 for needle Insecure Grasp, 0/20 and 17/20 for Post Misalignment, 6/10 and 9/10 for Shunt Disturbance, and 10/10 and 9/10 for Camera Freeze. Successful shunt rollouts have 6/20 fixed and 0/20 wrist false alarms.

The evaluation
contains 20 task-specific failure modes spanning four broad
categories:

Wrist-view FDR improves
from87.2%without action conditioning to88.8%with
action-token cross-attention and90.6%with global action
modulation, and then increases further to96.6%when both
mechanisms are used.

[paraphrase of V.B and Figure 6] K is varied over 1, 2, 3 and 4 while other architecture, calibration protocol and evaluation episodes are kept fixed. Wrist FDR is 42.2% at K=1 and 96.6% at K=4. Fixed-view FDR increases through K=3, then decreases slightly at K=4.

These rollouts cali-
brate thresholds under the deployment policy distribution and
support the exchangeability assumption used by conformal
prediction. Second, we use an episode-level threshold rather
than a time-varying conformal band as in FAILDetect [13].

Rather than reasoning about
task progress, surgical intent, or procedural correctness, the
proposed world-model score detects local inconsistencies
between commanded actions and observed visual dynam-
ics.

No separate representation-quality evaluation establishes L0, matched alternative-command comparison establishes L3, or model-coupled optimizer establishes L4. Unknown is not a finding that this is not a world model.

gate_assessments.rationale: Source/preprocessing roles and calibration-test disjointness are partly documented; variable-level provenance and dependence/model-selection audits are incomplete.
Implemented persistent learned transitions are supported; future-state fidelity results are not reported.
This operation produces a single endpoint per window, not a multi-time generated trajectory. Separate K configurations do not establish sequence rollout.
Alarm calibration/FAR is evaluated, but uncertainty-qualified acceptance and transfer exchangeability are unresolved. Endpoint-distribution calibration is separately unreported.
Commands condition dynamics; action contract/support and specified-action prediction fidelity remain insufficient.
No identified intervention-effect interpretation is made for the scoped alarm.
No model-coupled optimizer/policy is implemented; ACT is separately imitation-trained.
For the proposed safety-monitoring purpose, alarms are evaluated but hard blocking, abstention and response/fallback evidence remain unestablished.
Bounded OOD/fault testing does not establish independent clinical/site/camera transfer or validated alarm fusion.
No measured human usability or matched sim-to-real agreement claim is made in this scope. Physical hardware contributes R1, not those distinct outcomes.
The assessed use explicitly excludes online intervention and does not claim measured prospective patient/workflow benefit.
No defined operational release is documented; future research-asset release is not operational deployment.

legacy_cells.EG: Scoring frequency 13.98 Hz on a desktop workstation; the paper reports this exceeds the 10 Hz policy/observation loop.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared against observation-level anomaly baselines logpZO and RND; the paper reports FoMo-FD's WM-NC score outperformed both.
legacy_cells.EJ: WM-PE uses the same world model but scores endpoint prediction error; the paper reports the proposed inverse-transport WM-NC score performed substantially better.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations varied action-conditioning mode (none, global modulation, action-token cross-attention, both) and endpoint horizon K∈{1,2,3,4}.
legacy_cells.EL: Twenty task-specific failure modes were evaluated, including needle drop/slippage, insecure grasp, blood occlusion, ring drop, tissue grasp loss/disturbance, needle intrusion, insertion misalignment, and camera freeze.
legacy_cells.EM: Runtime failure monitoring with view-specific nonconformity scores and conformal thresholds calibrated on successful executions; alarms are raised when the score exceeds the threshold.
legacy_cells.FL: Frozen DINOv2 encodes fixed- and wrist-camera observations; per-view β-VAEs compress features into latent tensors; a transformer flow-matching model predicts an endpoint latent conditioned on latent history and the intervening robot action chunk; inverse transport scores the realized endpoint and conformal thresholds produce failure alarms. No planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces FoMo-FD, an action-conditioned flow-matching model of nominal short-horizon surgical visual dynamics and a conformally calibrated window-level failure detector trained without failure demonstrations.
legacy_cells.FN: Across four manipulation tasks and 20 failure modes, wrist-view WM-NC achieved 96.6% failure detection rate at 1.3% false alarm rate; scoring frequency was 13.98 Hz.
legacy_cells.FO: Successful policy rollouts are still required for conformal calibration; the study uses an episode-level rather than time-varying conformal threshold.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work includes progress- or state-conditioned calibration, combining local and global visual alarms, and integration with task-level monitors.
legacy_cells.FQ: Existing visual anomaly scores assess individual frames/embeddings rather than whether a short observation sequence evolves consistently with commanded actions; action-only signals can miss visual or execution mismatch failures.
legacy_cells.FR: Demonstrates offline failure detection on simulated and physical dVRK robot rollouts, not prospective clinical monitoring or online intervention; action conditioning and failure alarms do not establish causal treatment effects or safe autonomous control.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Calibrate nominal visual-action nonconformity on successful executions and expose task-specific alarms to a runtime safety gate.

limitations: Automated model review, not independent human verification, replication, clinical validation or authorization.
All nine text pages and earlier API image-review notes were supplied. Earlier page calls received images; this synthesis did not inspect images directly.
Source path/hash are supplied provenance, not recomputed or checked on disk. No external bibliographic, repository or release check was performed.
All 128 feature definitions received dispositions, with a separate endpoint-calibration scope. Programmatic schema/reference/KG validation was not executed.
The model ID denotes the reported experimental configuration, not an exact shared weights artifact. Task-specific checkpoint identities and exact DINOv2 variant are unreported.
Learned procedural endpoint dynamics are implemented, but future-state fidelity results and a separate L0 representation evaluation are not reported. Demonstrated L-level remains unknown.
Direct K-step endpoint supervision is not recursive rollout or traversal-based multi-step training. Legacy BW uses a broader target-based rule.
Robot timestep t, endpoint gap K, history L, window H and generative transport tau are distinct. No physical window duration or reciprocal latency was calculated.
Alarm scoring requires a completed observed window. Failure-onset-relative delay, early warning, live response and harm prevention are not reported.
Inverse-base distance is a nonconformity score, not an established clinical failure probability or exact conditional log likelihood.
Episode-maximum conformal alarm calibration is not calibration of endpoint probabilities or generated future-state trajectories. Aleatoric/epistemic components are not separated.
Nominal alpha=0.05 differs from observed FAR 10.0% fixed and 1.3% wrist. No uncertainty-qualified acceptance analysis establishes a general calibration pass/fail.
Fixed and wrist detectors are independent; joint guarantees, alarm fusion and clinical/camera/policy transfer are not established.
Expert-demonstration counts, command dimensions/units/frames, operator/session/material dependence, model size, solver settings and training compute are insufficiently reported.
The same evaluation episodes are used across K settings; independence of architecture/horizon selection is unreported.
Different simulated and physical tasks do not establish matched sim-to-real agreement. Physical material is not classified as human, animal, ex-vivo or a specific phantom type without provenance.
Held-out robot executions support R1, not R2 actual human/clinical validation. Expert teleoperation is not a human reader/use evaluation.
Fault challenges reveal missed detections and false alarms but do not establish exhaustive hazard coverage, a fully specified injection protocol or a security threat model.
Pooled rates mix task sample sizes. Detector comparisons do not uniformly match observed FAR; fixed WM-NC improves FDR over fixed RND while also having higher FAR.
The independently imitation-trained ACT host does not establish WM-coupled control, detector autonomy or evaluated intervention utility.
Hard guards, abstention, stop, escalation, privacy/security controls, ethics documentation and operational lifecycle governance remain insufficiently reported.
Assets are promised upon acceptance; actual accessibility, separate licenses and independent reproduction are not established.
References [1]–[31] were read as bibliography/context, not retrieved primary studies. Their planning, human-study and clinical capabilities are not inherited.
Earlier image notes contain chunk-local unavailable-page caveats; those do not describe the combined nine-page input.
Approximate graph readings and reviewer arithmetic in earlier notes are not promoted to source-reported metrics. Table paraphrases rely on the supplied prior image transcription plus full text.
